title: Cleaning text and rows
summary: Exports are reports, not tables: title rows on top, a total at the bottom, group labels written once, untidy names and repeated lines. Power Query fixes each with one step, and the fix runs again every month.
objectives: Remove report rows above the data and promote the headings.
Fill a group label down, after turning empty text into null.
Trim, clean and capitalise text, and know that Trim keeps inner double spaces.
Remove total rows and duplicates, and replace values.

p: A system report has a title, a date line and a blank line before the headings, and a Grand Total at the end. Remove Top Rows drops the first three; Use First Row as Headers promotes the headings; a filter removes the total.
Home › Remove Rows › Remove Top Rows: type the count.
Then Home › Use First Row as Headers.
Filter the total out by name, not by position, so a longer month still works.
In real life: has the same three lines on top every month. One step removes them for good.

p: The report writes each branch once, on the first row of its group. Fill Down copies a value into the empty cells below it. It fills null, not empty text, so turn the blanks into null first.
A CSV’s empty cells arrive as "" (empty text).
Replace Values: Value To Find empty, Replace With `null`.
Then Transform › Fill › Down.
In real life: filled nothing: the blanks were empty text. Replacing them with null made Fill Down work.

p: Transform › Format cleans text. Trim removes spaces at the start and end, Clean removes invisible characters, Capitalize Each Word fixes capitals. Unlike Excel’s TRIM, Power Query’s Trim keeps double spaces inside.
Excel’s TRIM also squeezes inner spaces; Text.Trim doesn’t.
Replace Values "  " with " " fixes double spaces.
Format › Trim on a whole column writes `Text.Trim`.
In real life: and “Patel Light House” were two customers in Neha’s pivot until the double space went.

p: Replace Values swaps text inside cells, or whole cells with Match entire cell contents. On text columns it replaces every match inside the text; tick Match entire cell contents to replace only whole values.
Select the column first; Replace Values works on the selected columns.
Find text is case-sensitive.
Each replacement is a step: easy to undo.
In real life: maps branch codes to names with Replace Values for now. Module 4 shows a lookup table that scales.

real.title: Clean June’s branch report in Excel
steps: Download **branch-report-june.csv** (button below) and save it in a folder you’ll keep, such as Documents.
In Excel: Data › From Text/CSV, pick the file, then **Transform Data**.
Remove the top 3 rows and use the first row as headers.
Replace the empty Branch cells with null (Replace Values: find nothing, replace with **null**), then Fill Down Branch.
Filter out the **Grand Total** row; Trim and Capitalize Each Word on Customer; Remove Duplicates on Invoice; replace double spaces in Customer with one.
Rename the query **Branch Sales** (Query Settings › Name), then Home › Close & Load.
